description: Phase 4, honest head-to-head measurement + docs. Broaden the benchmark to real-world-shaped, jev-inspired local fixtures (a Google-Flights-shaped multi-field search, a Wikipedia-open flow, a hotel search/filter flow) built as deterministic loopback fixtures (NOT live sites). Measure WALL-CLOCK, STEP COUNT, and BROWSER ROUND TRIPS on the SAME fixtures with the fast loop OFF (before) and ON (after), and record REAL before/after numbers. Keep the harness's honest labeling (ops-coverage is a subsequence match, not precision; the independent final-page verify is the trust signal). Do NOT fabricate a jev head-to-head: jev needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY + a text-model key + Browser Harness + real Chrome and almost certainly cannot run in this sandbox; if it cannot, say so explicitly and instead prove laya's own before/after fast-path speedup with real numbers, then reason qualitatively about the jev comparison from the measured per-step costs (zero network in the decision path, no text-LLM round trip, fewer steps). Update README and docs/PLAN.md with evidence-labeled claims.
steps: Add local, deterministic fixtures under benchmark/fixtures/ (served by benchmark/server.mjs) that are jev-inspired but do NOT hit live sites: (a) a flights-shaped fixture (origin + destination + date fields + a search button that reveals a results marker), (b) a wikipedia-open-shaped fixture (a search box + a result link that navigates to an article page with a title marker), (c) a hotel-search/filter fixture (a search field + a few filter checkboxes + a results list with an openable property). Register matching tasks in benchmark/tasks.mjs following the existing shape (id/category/description/fixture/applies/assist(h)/autopilot(h)/verify(h)); each verify(h) must RE-PROBE the real DOM for a literal outcome.

Add a BEFORE/AFTER measurement mode to the benchmark harness (benchmark/compare.mjs and/or runner.mjs) OR a small dedicated script that runs the laya Autopilot (laya_run_goal) over the fast-path-eligible tasks TWICE: once with LAYA_FAST_LOOP unset (before) and once with LAYA_FAST_LOOP=true (after), capturing for each: wall-clock ms, step count, and browser round trips (reuse the harness's existing round-trip counting). Write the results into RESULTS.md/results.json with an explicit BEFORE vs AFTER table. Keep BENCH_RUNS configurable; run enough repetitions to report a stable median. Label the metric honestly (coverage, not precision; verify() is the trust signal).

Run `pnpm run build` then `pnpm run bench:compare` (installs benchmark/node_modules on first run; OPEN_INTERNET). Capture the REAL generated RESULTS.md before/after numbers. Also run `pnpm run bench` (offline vitest report) and confirm it stays green. If `pnpm run bench:compare` cannot complete in this environment (e.g. @playwright/mcp unavailable), fall back to the dedicated before/after script that uses only laya's own dist server + the fixture server (no @playwright/mcp dependency) so real laya before/after numbers are still produced; document exactly what ran.

Attempt to determine whether jev-ultrafast can run here: check for TYPESAFE_API_KEY / a text-model key / browser_harness / real Chrome. If it cannot run (expected), record the precise reason (missing key/dependency) and DO NOT fabricate any jev number. Provide the qualitative jev comparison reasoned from the measured laya per-step costs (local decision ms with no network RTT; deterministic goal-grammar fills with no text-LLM call; fewer steps via batching).

Update README.md: add a section explaining the fast browser loop (atomic snapshot, persistent node identity, freshness guard + occlusion hit-test, adaptive waits), the LAYA_FAST_LOOP / LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS flags and easy setup, and the honest benchmark methodology with the REAL before/after numbers (wall-clock, steps, round trips). Every claim carries a measured/inferred/guess label. NO em dashes.

Update docs/PLAN.md: add a new phase section (Phase 7 or similarly named) describing the fast browser loop design and the levers, and extend the VERIFIED/INFERRED/GUESSED ledger with EXACTLY what was run this session (the commands and the real numbers), the jev-runnability finding, and the Phase 0 spike note (whether @receptron/laya can express per-operation target heads - record VERIFIED/INFERRED from the engine.ts single-shared-target-list reality, and note it is independent of levers 1-5). NO em dashes.

Verify no scratch/venv/weights/download artifacts are staged: run `git status --porcelain --ignored` and confirm no *.onnx / *.onnx.data / model/ / .venv / benchmark/node_modules are committed (benchmark/node_modules must stay gitignored). Confirm the committed RESULTS.md/results.json/charts reflect the real recorded run.
acceptance_criteria: New jev-inspired local fixtures + tasks exist and their verify(h) re-probes the real DOM for a literal outcome.

RESULTS.md/results.json contain a REAL before (flag off) vs after (flag on) comparison of wall-clock, step count, and browser round trips on the SAME fixtures, generated by an actual run (not hand-written numbers).
The jev-runnability question is answered honestly with the precise blocker if it cannot run; no fabricated jev numbers.
README and docs/PLAN.md explain the fast path + flags + honest methodology, every claim labeled measured/inferred/guess, with NO em dashes.
pnpm run bench stays green; git status shows no committed weights/scratch/venv/node_modules.
verification: Run `pnpm run build` then the before/after measurement (`pnpm run bench:compare` or the dedicated laya-only script) and confirm RESULTS.md shows real before/after numbers.
Run `pnpm run bench` and confirm it stays green (domwalk + aria).
Run `git status --porcelain --ignored` and confirm no weights/scratch/venv/benchmark node_modules are staged.
Run `grep -rn "\xE2\x80\x94" README.md docs/PLAN.md` (em dash) and confirm no matches in new prose.
